q: What does a capability map describe?
options: Stable abilities an organization needs, independent of current teams and systems
why: Capabilities describe what the business must be able to do.

q: What does a value stream represent?
options: End-to-end stages through which a stakeholder receives value
why: Value streams show how work flows across handoffs to an outcome.

q: What is a good use of a capability map?
options: Compare gaps and investment needs at a useful level
why: Maps should support decisions, not serve as decoration.

q: What should current-state analysis combine?
options: Formal procedures, actual practice, data and control evidence
why: Real operations may differ from written process and should be validated.

q: Why define “aged break” consistently across regions?
options: Comparisons require the same population and calculation
It reduces the need for a target
It is only a technical concern
why: Metric definitions must be aligned before comparing performance.

q: How should a fixed constraint be distinguished from an assumption?
options: Verify its source and whether it can be changed
Treat every stakeholder statement as fixed
why: Some constraints are negotiable; others require evidence and authority.

q: What belongs in a target operating model?
options: Roles, processes, data, systems, controls and performance ownership
why: A target operating model describes how the organization will operate after change.

q: Why validate a target model with frontline users?
options: They can reveal whether responsibilities and processes work in practice
why: Operational validation catches gaps not visible to project leaders.

q: How should necessary regional variation be handled?
options: Define the global minimum and document justified local differences
Let each team invent its own terms
why: A deliberate model can standardize controls while preserving valid local needs.

q: What is a transition state?
options: An intermediate operating condition between current and target states
why: Transitions describe how the organization moves safely toward the target.

q: Why define exit criteria for a transition?
options: To know when it is safe to proceed to the next state
To guarantee the vendor is paid
To make the roadmap look complete
why: Exit criteria provide evidence for progression decisions.

q: What can coexistence of old and new systems create?
why: Transition planning must consider parallel systems and duplicate work.

q: What should a business architecture roadmap show?
options: Outcomes, capabilities, dependencies, timing and decision gates
Every coding task as a fixed promise
why: Roadmaps communicate sequencing and outcomes at the right level.

q: How should scenario planning be used?
options: Show how the roadmap changes under materially different assumptions
why: Scenario planning makes uncertainty and decision consequences visible.

q: What is a useful enabling work item?
options: Data cleanup required before safe matching automation
why: Enabling work can unlock later outcome delivery.

q: Why map ecosystem impacts?
options: Change can affect vendors, regulators, customers and adjacent teams
why: Enterprise changes often cross organizational boundaries.

q: What should be reviewed for a vendor-dependent process?
options: Service obligations, data handling, access, continuity and exit needs with proper owners
why: Vendor arrangements affect operations, privacy, resilience and accountability.

q: What should the BA do when a change affects another team's authority?
options: Identify the decision owner and bring the impact to that forum
why: Cross-boundary decisions need the right owner and timing.

q: How should current-state evidence be presented when sources disagree?
options: Show the disagreement, confidence and how it will be resolved
Pick the largest dataset without question
why: Transparency about evidence quality supports sound decisions.

q: What makes a roadmap useful?
options: It shows what outcomes come when and what decisions or dependencies matter
why: A roadmap supports prioritization and coordination.
